intended_object: This is the canonical comparison isomorphism H^n(f) ≅ H^n(cone(F.map f)) between the objects of the spectral object attached to a functor F : ι ⥤ CochainComplex C ℤ and the cohomology of the mapping cone of F.map f. I took this from the docstring and from how `spectralObject_δ` uses it.
explanation:
The declaration is not a mathematical object in its own right. It is an API isomorphism that lets the library unfold `spectralObject F` into concrete terms. It is used to state `spectralObject_δ`, which describes the connecting maps.

`spectralObject F` is obtained by applying the homology functor of the homotopy category to the mapping-cone triangulated spectral object. So `((spectralObject F).H n).obj (mk₁ f)` is, by definition, the homology in the homotopy category of the image of `mappingCone (F.map f)` (up to shifting by n).

The body uses Mathlib's `homologyFunctorFactors`, applied at `mappingCone (F.map f)`. This is the standard natural isomorphism saying that the quotient functor followed by homology on the homotopy category is the homology of complexes. This is exactly the canonical identification.

The construction is correct and matches its docstring. Its generality is that of the surrounding construction: any abelian C, any category ι, and ℤ-indexed cochain complexes, which mapping cones and triangulated structure need. Since it is a technical comparison isomorphism rather than a standalone notion, it falls under `not_a_mathematical_object`.
